title: Malachi Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Malachi chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Malachi Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Malachi Chapter 2.

questions.question: In Malachi 2, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
questions.explanation: The commandment for priests appears first as stated in Malachi 2:1.

questions.question: What will happen if the priests do not lay it to heart, according to Malachi 2?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:2 states that if the priests do not lay it to heart, the LORD will send a curse upon them.

questions.question: What does the LORD say He will spread upon the faces of the priests?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:3 mentions that the LORD will spread dung upon their faces.

questions.question: Who is the covenant mentioned in Malachi 2 associated with?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:4 states that the covenant is with Levi.

questions.question: What was the nature of the covenant with Levi?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:5 describes the covenant with Levi as one of life and peace.

questions.question: What was found in Levi's mouth according to Malachi 2?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:6 states that the law of truth was in Levi's mouth.

questions.question: What did Levi do that is mentioned in Malachi 2?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:6 indicates that Levi walked with the LORD in peace and equity.

questions.question: What will the LORD do to the blessings of the priests?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:2 states that the LORD will curse their blessings if they do not honor Him.

questions.question: How did Levi respond to the fear of the LORD?
questions.explanation: According to Malachi 2:5, Levi was afraid before the name of the LORD.

questions.question: What did Levi turn many away from according to Malachi 2?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:6 states that Levi turned many away from iniquity.

questions.question: The priests are commanded to give glory to whose name?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:2 specifies that the priests are to give glory unto the name of the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: The commandment in Malachi 2 is directed at the priests.
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:1 indicates that the commandment is specifically for the priests.

questions.question: True or False: The covenant with Levi was one of life and peace.
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:5 states that the covenant with Levi was indeed one of life and peace.

questions.question: True or False: The priests are told they will be rewarded for their blessings.
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:2 says the LORD will curse their blessings, not reward them.

questions.question: True or False: Levi was known for spreading lies according to Malachi 2.
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:6 states that iniquity was not found in Levi's lips, indicating he did not spread lies.

medium.title: Malachi Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Malachi Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What should the priest's lips keep according to Malachi 2:7?
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'For the priest's lips should keep knowledge' (Malachi 2:7).

questions.question: What does Malachi 2:2 promise will happen if the priests do not lay it to heart?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:2 states, 'I will even send a curse upon you,' indicating that failure to heed the command leads to a curse.

questions.question: What has caused many to stumble at the law according to Malachi 2:8?
options: The priests' departure from the way
questions.correctAnswer: The priests' departure from the way
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'But ye are departed out of the way; ye have caused many to stumble at the law' (Malachi 2:8).

questions.question: What is the consequence mentioned in Malachi 2:9 for those who have not kept God's ways?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:9 says, 'Therefore have I also made you contemptible and base before all the people,' showing the consequence of not keeping God's ways.

questions.question: According to Malachi 2:10, what commonality do all people have?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:10 states, 'Have we not all one father?' indicating the shared fatherhood among all people.

questions.question: What does Malachi 2:11 say about Judah's actions?
options: They have profaned the holiness of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They have profaned the holiness of the LORD
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Judah hath profaned the holiness of the LORD which he loved,' indicating their wrongdoing.

questions.question: What does Malachi 2:12 say will happen to the man who does treacherously?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:12 states, 'The LORD will cut off the man that doeth this,' indicating a severe consequence for treachery.

questions.question: How does Malachi 2:7 define the role of the priest?
questions.explanation: The verse describes the priest as 'the messenger of the LORD of hosts' (Malachi 2:7).

questions.question: What is a key theme in Malachi 2:8 regarding the law?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:8 mentions that they 'have corrupted the covenant of Levi,' indicating a corruption of the law.

questions.question: What does Malachi 2:10 imply about brotherhood?
questions.explanation: The verse raises the question, 'why do we deal treacherously every man against his brother?' indicating the significance of brotherhood.

questions.question: What does Malachi 2:9 reveal about partiality in the law?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'ye have not kept my ways, but have been partial in the law,' highlighting that partiality is wrong.

questions.question: What does Malachi 2:11 say about intermarriage with strange gods?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:11 declares that 'an abomination is committed in Israel and in Jerusalem,' condemning such intermarriage.

questions.question: According to Malachi 2:3, what will God do to those who do not honor Him?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:3 states, 'Behold, I will corrupt your seed,' indicating a curse for dishonoring God.

questions.question: Is it true that Malachi 2:5 speaks about a covenant of wealth?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:5 refers to a covenant of 'life and peace,' not wealth.

questions.question: According to Malachi 2:6, did Levi walk with God in peace and equity?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:6 states that Levi indeed walked with God in peace and equity, making this statement true.

hard.title: Malachi Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Malachi Chapter 2.

questions.question: According to Malachi 2:13, what has been done to the altar of the LORD?
options: Covered with tears, weeping, and crying out
questions.correctAnswer: Covered with tears, weeping, and crying out
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:13 states that the altar of the LORD has been covered with tears, with weeping, and with crying out, indicating sorrow rather than acceptance of offerings.

questions.question: In Malachi 2:14, why does the LORD say the people have dealt treacherously?
options: Because they have been unfaithful to the wife of their youth
Because they have not brought offerings
Because they have worshiped idols openly
Because they have neglected the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Because they have been unfaithful to the wife of their youth
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:14 explains that the LORD has been witness between the people and the wife of their youth, against whom they have dealt treacherously by being unfaithful.

questions.question: What is the purpose of making 'one' according to Malachi 2:15?
options: That he might seek a godly seed
That he might build a temple
questions.correctAnswer: That he might seek a godly seed
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:15 states that God made one so that he might seek a godly seed, emphasizing the importance of faithfulness and godly offspring.

questions.question: What does the LORD say about 'putting away' in Malachi 2:16?
options: He is indifferent to putting away
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:16 clearly states that the LORD hates putting away, referring to divorce or abandonment, and warns to take heed to one's spirit.

questions.question: In Malachi 2:17, what complaint do the people make about the LORD?
options: They say He delights in those who do evil
They say He rewards only the righteous
They say He is silent in judgment
They say He is slow to punish
questions.correctAnswer: They say He delights in those who do evil
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:17 presents the complaint that the people say every one who doeth evil is good in the sight of the LORD and that He delights in them, questioning the justice of God.

questions.question: Why does the LORD no longer regard the offering with good will at your hand in Malachi 2:13?
options: Because the altar is covered with tears and weeping
Because the priests have not consecrated the offerings
Because the people have not fasted
questions.correctAnswer: Because the altar is covered with tears and weeping
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:13 explains that the LORD does not regard the offering with good will because the altar is covered with tears, weeping, and crying out, indicating insincere worship.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'putting away' (Malachi 2:16) mean?
options: Divorce or dismissal of a wife
questions.correctAnswer: Divorce or dismissal of a wife
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'putting away' in Malachi 2:16 refers to divorce or dismissal of a wife, which God declares He hates.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Malachi 2:13 with the phrase 'covering the altar of the LORD with tears'?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:13 uses metaphor by describing the altar as being 'covered with tears,' representing sorrow and insincere worship rather than literal tears on the altar.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of faithfulness in marriage as found in Malachi 2:14?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 5:31 echoes the theme in Malachi 2:14 where marriage is described as two becoming one flesh, emphasizing faithfulness and covenant relationship.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the covenant theme between God and Levi found in Malachi 2:4-6?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 33:8-11 blesses Levi and speaks of the priestly covenant, connecting closely with Malachi 2:4-6's references to the covenant with Levi.

questions.question: What verse precedes Malachi 2:13 and introduces the issue of Judah's treachery?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:12 precedes 2:13 and discusses Judah profaning the holiness of the LORD and marrying the daughter of a strange god, setting the context for the following verses.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'the residue of the spirit' in Malachi 2:15 from a theological perspective?
options: It implies the leftover part of the divine spirit enabling unity
It describes a ritual cleansing process
It refers to the physical descendants of Levi
questions.correctAnswer: It implies the leftover part of the divine spirit enabling unity
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:15 refers to 'the residue of the spirit' indicating the divine presence or spirit remaining after creation, enabling the unity of man and wife for a godly seed.

questions.question: How does Malachi 2:17 illustrate the use of rhetorical questioning?
options: It uses questions to challenge the people's misunderstanding of God's justice
It uses questions to praise the LORD's mercy
It uses questions to introduce a new covenant
It uses questions to describe temple rituals
questions.correctAnswer: It uses questions to challenge the people's misunderstanding of God's justice
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:17 employs rhetorical questions to confront the people's erroneous claims that God delights in evil, thereby highlighting their spiritual complacency.

questions.question: How does Malachi 2:7 describe the role of the priest in relation to the law?
options: The priest should keep knowledge and seek the law at his mouth
The priest should offer sacrifices only
The priest should build the temple
The priest should ignore the law
questions.correctAnswer: The priest should keep knowledge and seek the law at his mouth
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:7 explains that the priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth because he is the messenger of the LORD.

questions.question: According to Malachi 2:10, what is the underlying reason for dealing treacherously against one's brother?
options: Profaning the covenant of our fathers
questions.correctAnswer: Profaning the covenant of our fathers
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:10 states that dealing treacherously against one's brother is profaning the covenant of our fathers, highlighting the breach of a sacred familial and communal bond.

theological.title: Malachi Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Malachi Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Malachi 2:2 teach about God's response to human disobedience?
options: God actively curses those who refuse to honor His name
God passively allows consequences without direct intervention
God rewards disobedience to teach mercy
God ignores the disobedient to test their faith
questions.correctAnswer: God actively curses those who refuse to honor His name
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:2 clearly states that the LORD will send a curse upon the priests who do not give glory to His name, indicating active divine judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine about the priesthood is taught in Malachi 2:7?
options: Priests are messengers of God who must preserve and teach His law
Priests are primarily political leaders in Israel
Priests should seek personal gain rather than public instruction
Priests are independent from God's covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Priests are messengers of God who must preserve and teach His law
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:7 identifies the priest as the messenger who must keep knowledge and seek the law at God's mouth, emphasizing their role as teachers and covenant mediators.

questions.question: What doctrine about the covenant with Levi is affirmed in Malachi 2:5?
options: God's covenant with Levi was established on the basis of life and peace
The covenant with Levi was conditional on military success
Levi's covenant was based on wealth and power
The covenant was annulled due to Levi's disobedience
questions.correctAnswer: God's covenant with Levi was established on the basis of life and peace
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:5 states that God's covenant with Levi was of life and peace, given to him because of his fear and reverence for God.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Malachi 2:4 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:4 emphasizes that God sent a commandment to uphold His covenant with Levi, demonstrating His faithfulness to His promises.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is illustrated in Malachi 2:16 regarding God's attitude toward divorce?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:16 reveals that the LORD hates putting away (divorce), reflecting His holy standard regarding covenant faithfulness in marriage.

questions.question: How does Malachi 2:11 relate to the broader biblical theme of idolatry and covenant unfaithfulness?
options: It highlights Judah's betrayal by marrying foreign women, symbolizing spiritual unfaithfulness
It encourages intermarriage to promote unity
It denies any connection between marriage and covenant faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights Judah's betrayal by marrying foreign women, symbolizing spiritual unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:11 indicates that Judah committed an abomination by marrying daughters of strange gods, which reflects covenant unfaithfulness consistent with themes in Exodus and Deuteronomy.

questions.question: In what way does Malachi 2:13 prepare for New Testament teaching on worship and sincerity?
options: By condemning insincere offerings that are rejected by God
By promoting ritual sacrifice over heartfelt worship
By separating worship from ethical behavior
By teaching that God accepts any offerings regardless of attitude
questions.correctAnswer: By condemning insincere offerings that are rejected by God
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:13 describes offerings covered with tears and weeping that God no longer regards with favor, paralleling New Testament emphasis on sincere worship (e.g., John 4:24).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Malachi 2:14 and 2:15 teach about marriage and sanctification?
options: Marriage is a covenant designed by God to produce a godly seed
Marriage is a social contract with no spiritual significance
Marriage is primarily for economic advantage
questions.correctAnswer: Marriage is a covenant designed by God to produce a godly seed
questions.explanation: Verses 2:14-15 emphasize marriage as a covenant witnessed by God, intended to seek a godly seed, highlighting sanctification through covenant fidelity.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Malachi 2:8 and 2:9 teach about covenant violation and its consequences?
options: Corrupting the covenant leads to public disgrace and loss of honor
Violation of the covenant is overlooked by God if repentance is delayed
Breaking the covenant results in immediate physical death
Covenant violation has no social consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Corrupting the covenant leads to public disgrace and loss of honor
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:8-9 describes how priests who corrupt the covenant become contemptible before the people, showing social and divine consequences of covenant unfaithfulness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Malachi 2:10 and 2:11 teach about God's design for unity and the sin of treachery among His people?
options: God created all from one Father, thus treachery against brothers violates divine unity
God approves division among His people for cultural diversity
God’s covenant allows for treachery if politically beneficial
Treachery is neutral in God’s eyes as long as religious rituals continue
questions.correctAnswer: God created all from one Father, thus treachery against brothers violates divine unity
questions.explanation: Verses 2:10-11 emphasize that all have one Father and that treachery among brothers profanes the covenant, underscoring God's desire for unity and faithfulness.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Malachi 2:17 suggests God condones evil by saying the LORD delights in evildoers. What does Malachi 2:17 actually teach?
options: The people falsely accuse God of delighting in evil, but He does not
God is indifferent to human sin
questions.correctAnswer: The people falsely accuse God of delighting in evil, but He does not
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:17 records the people's cynical claim, but the context shows their error in accusing God, revealing their misunderstanding, not God's endorsement.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine judgment is taught in Malachi 2:12?
options: God will cut off those who profane the covenant, both leaders and learners
God only judges the laypeople, sparing leaders
questions.correctAnswer: God will cut off those who profane the covenant, both leaders and learners
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:12 declares that the LORD will cut off the master and scholar who profane the covenant, emphasizing God’s impartial judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Malachi 2:6 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:6 states that in Levi’s mouth was the law of truth and no iniquity was found, demonstrating God's holy standard reflected through His covenant servant.

questions.question: How does Malachi 2:3 contribute to the narrative arc of God's judgment on unfaithful priests in Scripture?
options: It graphically describes the corruption and disgrace that will come upon disobedient priests
It promises immediate restoration regardless of sins
It ignores the role of priests in covenant fidelity
It absolves priests from consequences due to their office
questions.correctAnswer: It graphically describes the corruption and disgrace that will come upon disobedient priests
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:3 speaks of corrupting the seed and spreading dung on faces, illustrating the severe judgment on unfaithful priests, consistent with the prophetic theme of priestly accountability.

questions.question: What combined theological principle is taught by Malachi 2:14 and 2:16 concerning covenant faithfulness and human spirit?
options: God requires faithfulness in marriage and warns against treachery in spirit
Covenant faithfulness is optional and human spirit is irrelevant
God values only ritual compliance, not faithfulness
Divorce is encouraged as a remedy for covenant breach
questions.correctAnswer: God requires faithfulness in marriage and warns against treachery in spirit
questions.explanation: Verses 2:14 and 2:16 teach that God is witness to the marriage covenant and hates putting away, urging people to guard their spirit against treachery.
